items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: My first well of course Mary Lou Williams and all those boogie woogie guys that — my dad got me these albums — Pinetop Smith and Albert Ammons, and Meade Lux Lewis and on and on. So that really influenced me.

ctx.x: Okay. Did you have major influences on the piano? People that you —

How many hours do we have here? My first well of course Mary Lou Williams and all those boogie woogie guys that — my dad got me these albums — Pinetop Smith and Albert Ammons, and Meade Lux Lewis and on and on. So that really influenced me. But this guy, this guy who I met when I was a junior in high school played a couple of things for me. He played a man named Jimmy Yancy, who, you know if I had to have only one influence that would be it. And it sounds so simple, what he does. And I truly believe in making…
What attracts you to do somebody else’s songs?
